name: palak paneer
instructions:
SINGLE VARIANT NOW (the two-variant fork is collapsed — see notes). Spinach + fried paneer + roasted vegetables + indian spices + lime. CURRY POWDER + CARDAMOM is king, with CARDAMOM the most important spice.

=== THE SPINACH — DICED OR WHOLE LEAVES ===

Washed and cut (or whole); braised in the pan, eaten as individual leaves. No pestle, never blended (babyfood spinach).

=== SPICE STACK ===

CURRY POWDER + CARDAMOM (king — cardamom is the most important spice), cumin, coriander, AJWAIN, THYME, turmeric, chili powder, kashmiri chili powder, red chili flakes, amchur powder. NO garam masala, NO cinnamon/fennel/cloves (see notes). Shawarma spice is an additional option (secondary).

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. CUBE AND FRY THE PANEER — DO THIS FIRST, ALWAYS, BEFORE THE SPICES GO IN: shallow-fry in olive oil until golden; set aside. Paneer releases no moisture — a masala built first scorches under it (the spices burn); frying first also leaves paneer-flavored oil for the masala.
2. PREP THE VEGETABLES: roast the cauliflower (florets in vegetable oil, salt, a pinch of turmeric, 425°F until browned and crispy); oven-roast the peppers (poblano/jalapeño — never sautéed, see notes); parboil the turnips/rutabaga (cubed, salted water, just-tender — same treatment the potatoes got).
3. BLOOM the spices in the residual olive oil; sauté the GARLIC briefly (no ginger, no onion).
4. QUICKLY ADD WATER to prevent burning.
5. Add the WASHED/CUT SPINACH LEAVES and BRAISE UNTIL DRY-ISH.
6. Add the PRECOOKED components AFTER: fried paneer, roasted cauliflower + peppers, parboiled roots, toasted pumpkin/sunflower seeds.
7. Generous squeeze of fresh LIME (non-negotiable); LEMON JUICE to brighten is good too; salt LIGHTLY (the paneer salt note).

=== WRAP APPLICATION ===

Tastes good in a TORTILLA/NAAN WRAP, BAKED IN THE OVEN AFTER filling (see notes).
notes:
SINGLE VARIANT NOW: the old two-variant structure (A: potato + cauliflower + soft cheese + ghee; B: paneer + olive oil) is collapsed into ONE dish — the paneer build, with the roasted-vegetable slot folded in. Ghee, feta, and monterrey jack stay PRIMARY in the merged dish; potatoes and bell peppers are secondary.

TOFU IS CLASHING — BLAND WITH THE SPINACH: a tofu version doesn't work; it's bland against the spinach. (Same unloaded-carrier failure recorded in [[mint-cilantro-chicken]] — tofu earns its place in indian cooking only loaded, like the yogurt-marinade-and-broil of [[tikka-masala]]. Here the paneer is the flavor.)

SPINACH — DICED OR WHOLE LEAVES, STEAMED AT THE END (PESTLE WALKED BACK): I dislike the pestled spinach — walked back. This is a good recipe for DICED OR WHOLE SPINACH LEAVES, steamed in at the end, so they can be EATEN MORE INDIVIDUALLY as a component. (The blender-and-coconut approach stays dead too — no green goos.) Mixed greens work in a pinch but read lighter — reach for them only with no spinach on hand. Never blend, food-process, or pestle.

=== CURRY POWDER + CARDAMOM IS KING — CARDAMOM THE MOST IMPORTANT SPICE ===

CURRY POWDER + CARDAMOM is still the ruling combination, and CARDAMOM FEELS LIKE THE MOST IMPORTANT SPICE in the dish. Use it generously — it's the spice that ties the dish to its indian-saag identity, balancing the fried-paneer richness with a warm floral background. (A spice I'd been dosing too lightly for years.)

=== GARAM MASALA IS OUT; CINNAMON/FENNEL/CLOVES ARE OUT ===

GARAM MASALA is out of the stack, and the warm-sweet spices — CINNAMON, FENNEL, CLOVES — are out with it. All marked clashing. SHAWARMA spice is in as an additional spice option (secondary).

=== AROMATICS — GARLIC IN, GINGER OUT, ONIONS CLASHING ===

GARLIC is in. GINGER is out — left out of the dish entirely. ONIONS remain one of the few indian dishes where they're inappropriate — most of the family (chana masala, rajma, tikka masala) requires a sautéed onion base; palak paneer reads better without: redundant sweetness plus a caramelized bass note the dense spinach + paneer composition doesn't want. Yellow, red, and white onions all clashing; scallions and shallots stay out by default.

=== THE VEGETABLE SLOT — LESS-WESTERN ROOTS AND PEPPERS ARE PRIMARY ===

TURNIP, POBLANO, JALAPEÑO, and RUTABAGA are the PRIMARY vegetables — they taste LESS WESTERN in the finished product. POTATO and BELL PEPPER are demoted to SECONDARY for the same reason in reverse. CAULIFLOWER is in (primary).

Prep rules carried over: CAULIFLOWER CRISPY-BAKED (oil + salt + pinch of turmeric, 425°F until browned — steamed or raw-added goes limp). PEPPERS OVEN-ROASTED, NEVER SAUTÉED — sautéed peppers read too mediterranean; roasted keeps the indian roast-and-braise language. ROOTS (turnip/rutabaga, or potato if using) PARBOILED — cubed, salted water, just-tender, so they hold shape in the masala.

=== FRY THE PANEER FIRST — BEFORE THE SPICES, SO THEY DON'T BURN ===

Paneer doesn't release much liquid when it hits the pan. If you build the masala first and THEN add raw paneer, the garlic and spices scorch on the pan bottom before the paneer has any moisture to protect them. Order matters:
1. Fry the paneer cubes first in olive oil until golden. Set aside.
2. THEN build the masala in the same pan with residual oil (now paneer-flavored — a bonus).
3. Add the fried paneer back at the end alongside the spinach.
This is unique to paneer as a protein — a chicken variant would have surface moisture to protect the masala. Not paneer.

THE FAT: olive oil (or vegetable oil) for frying the paneer and the masala; GHEE is also primary. (The old paneer variant's skip-the-ghee rule — paneer + ghee reads overly rich — came from the two-variant era; ghee is back in the merged dish.)

PANEER IS ALREADY SALTY — SALT-BY-SAUCE-TASTE MISLEADS: easy to oversalt by tasting the sauce alone — the paneer carries its own salt. Salt light; judge by a bite WITH paneer in it.

=== AJWAIN + THYME ARE PRIMARY ===

Ajwain (carom) and thyme both have a thyme-and-oregano-adjacent character that pairs cleanly with fried paneer's dairy-fried surface — paneer + ajwain + thyme is one of the more distinctive combinations in this dish family. Toss the thyme into the ground spice mix alongside the ajwain. (The old restraint warning was specific to the retired feta-potato variant and goes with it.)

=== THE CHILE STACK ===

Generic chili powder + KASHMIRI chili powder + RED CHILI FLAKES are all necessary — same rule as [[mint-cilantro-chicken]]:
- KASHMIRI: bright red color, gentle warming heat. Non-optional.
- FLAKES: whole-form chile presence, bloomed in the oil at the masala stage.
- GENERIC CHILI POWDER: broad heat + earthy character.
Fresh chile now also lives in the vegetable slot — roasted poblano and jalapeño are primary.

=== TOASTED PUMPKIN/SUNFLOWER SEEDS — ALWAYS NICE (WHOLE, NOT MASHED) ===

Toasted pumpkin and/or sunflower seeds are always nice — cooked with the paneer, never pestled. Whole toasted seeds riding with the structural components.

=== LIME IS REQUIRED — NON-NEGOTIABLE; LEMON JUICE TO BRIGHTEN IS GOOD ===

The lime finish is what makes the recipe cohere — brightness against the dairy fat and earthy spices. Squeeze fresh and generously at the finish. LEMON JUICE added to brighten is also good — lemon is in. (This reverses the old lemon-is-clashing stance from the two-variant era.)

=== WRAP APPLICATION — TORTILLA/NAAN WRAP, BAKED AFTER ===

Tastes good in a TORTILLA OR NAAN WRAP, BAKED IN THE OVEN AFTER filling. The paneer-plus-spinach composition reads gratin-adjacent, and the lime + chili powder read especially well in this format. If making tortillas from scratch, see the flour tortillas recipe.
